name: Parking and Traffic Commission Meeting
agenda_text:
CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION (PTC)
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A

  JULY 2024 AGENDA

Barbara Hibler, Chairperson  Peter Puglese, City Traffic Engineer
Richard Galindo, District 1  Diana Maximo, Parking and Traffic Department
Kip Rudd, District 2  William Thompson, Parking and Traffic Department
Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3  Lieutenant David Salcedo, Police Department
Lois Hale, District 4

Rules of Decorum: https://www.cityofinglewood.org/DocumentCenter/View/18857/2023-Rules-of-Decorum

A. OPENING CEREMONIES
1. Roll Call

B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEMS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any item on the agenda, other than the
  Public Hearing, may do so at this time.

C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1. Approval of the Minutes for the Meeting held on June 27, 2024.

D. UNFINISHED BUSINESS
1. City-owned parking facilities as parking meter zones with special event parking rates and fines. Options being
  studied for implementing event parking rates/fines for public parking lots. To view and read the staff report
  click on the link https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/16627?fileID=23655
a. Requesting a Status Update

2. Implementation of event parking rates/fines for on-street parking meters on Manchester Boulevard between
  Prairie Avenue and La Brea Avenue.
a. Requesting a Status Update

E. NEW BUSINESS
1. Commissioner Richard Galindo requested a list of all traffic signal lights controlled and locations by the City
  of Inglewood. Appendix A provides requested information

F. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City business
  not elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

G. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
1. The members of the Parking and Traffic Commission will provide oral reports, including reports on City
  related travels where lodging expenses are incurred, and/or address any matters they deem of general
  interest to the public.

H. ANNOUNCEMENTS
1. The next Parking and Traffic Commission meeting will be held on Wednesday, August 28, 2024 at 7:00
  p.m., First Floor, City Hall Community Room A, Inglewood City Hall One Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA
  90301.

I. ADJOURNMENT

   CITY OF INGLEWOOD

  City Hall Lobby Community Room A

  JULY JUNE 2024 MEETING MINUTES

A. OPENING CEREMONIES
1. Meeting was held at 7:02 pm (PST) in the Community Room A located in the first floor on 06/26/24
2. Attendees included Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett Roberts, Lois Hale, Diana
  Maximo, and Lieutenant Fernandez

B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEM
1. There were no comments from persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on
  any agenda item.

C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1. Approval of the Minutes for the Meeting held on May 22, 2024.
a. The information appears on pages 3-7 of the agenda for June 26, 2024. To view the agenda click
  on the link: https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_06262024-4120
b. The first motion to accept was made by Commissioner Rudd and seconded by Commissioner
  Galindo.
c. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote: Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd
  and Lois Hale. Brett Roberts abstains from participating.
d. Four of the five members agreed with the motion to approve the minutes.

D. UNFINISHED BUSINESS
1. City-owned parking facilities as parking meter zones with special event parking rates and fines. To
  view the staff report click on the link, https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/16627?fileID=23655
a. Oral status report on the City-owned parking facilities was requested.
b. It was informed to the Commission that no discussion activity had occurred or fact data to provide
  at the moment. The Department of Parking and Traffic is still discussing the matter internally.
c. Commissioner Rudd reminded that the concerns is public parking for residents. For example, how
  the parking space at event time will be distinguished from non-event or regular parking. Signage
  and public parking for residents during the events were also highlighted.
d. Diana Maximo indicated that working with citizens during implementation will be the main objective
  when enforcing the plan.
e. Commission Rudd recommended bringing the matter to the Parking and Traffic Commission for
  review and comment before presenting the report to the City Council.
f. The subject will be discussed at the next meeting.

E. NEW BUSINESS
1. Commissioner Rudd opened discussion on implementing event parking fees/fines for on-street
  meters on Manchester Boulevard between Prairie Avenue and La Brea Avenue.
a. The Commission was informed that there will be signage on the meter to notify the public.
b. With two hours in advance, the meter rate will change during the event but everything will depend
  on the even type.
c. Parking Enforcement Officers will be trained on how to implement parking fees and fines.
d. This is just a pilot test and more will be learned later about the success of the plan.
e. The subject will be discussed at the next meeting.

JUNE 2024_PTC COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  -1-
   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION (PTC)
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A

  JULY JUNE 2024 MEETING MINUTES

2. Requesting a presentation on expanded scope of services for parking enforcement.
a. Staff report recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment No. 2 to
  Agreement No. 14-142 with LAZ Karp Associates, LLC (LAZ), extending the contract from June 1,
  2024, to May 31, 2029; modifying the scope of services; and increasing the maximum annual
  compensation. Click to view https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/17247?fileID=24286
b. The Commission was informed that the plan is to double the number of parking enforcement officers
  on duty, which will allow for assigned patrol beats, daily meter monitoring and additional parking
  enforcement officers to handle unique details such as local school traffic. In addition, the agreement
  allows hourly rates to be increased to align them with inflation and make them competitive in terms
  of parking and traffic control.
c. The subject will not be discussed at the next meeting. The Commission was satisfied with the
  explanation given.

F. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.
a. A resident of 85th Street raised the issue of non-resident parking on the street to attend an event.
  The resident asked about the citywide implementation of the Residential Parking Permit Program
  and why the city has not visited the site to ticket the vehicles.
 The resident was informed that those vehicles had obtained a day pass for parking during events
  where the City cannot take any action to prevent congestion.
b. A Crenshaw Boulevard resident raised the issues of trash day.
 Concern was noted that no sweeping is being done in the alley area.
 City Staff agreed to forward the request to the appropriate department to assist the resident in
  resolving the issue.

G. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
1. The members of the Parking and Traffic Commission will provide oral reports, including reports on
  City related travels where lodging expenses are incurred, and/or address any matters they deem of
  general interest to the public.
a. Chairwoman Barbara Hibler urged all commissioners to notify their attendance prior to the meeting
  to ensure a full forum.Chairwoman Barbara Hibler asked the Police Department to provide an
  update on how the city is doing.
 The Police Department notified the Commission that the main incidents faced by police were break-
  ins, homicides, and traffic accidents due to construction.
 An observation was made on the new island installed in the City by the Lieutenant. The new island
  was said to have served as a barrier during vehicle chases.
 The lieutenant also stated that the traffic light cycle time appears to be longer after traffic has been
  directed to the specific entertainment center.
 City Staff agreed to share the message on the matter with the city's traffic engineer.
b. Commissioner Lois Hale stated that the streets are not cleaned after the event.
 City staff agreed to share the message regarding the matter with the appropriate person within
  Public Works.

  JULY JUNE 2024 MEETING MINUTES

c. Commissioner Kip Rudd requests adding a new business item to the August agenda to discuss
  signage around the whole City.
 City Staff agreed to add the item to the August agenda.

H. ANNOUNCEMENTS
1. It was announced that the next Traffic and Parking Commission meeting will be Wednesday, July
  24, 2024 at 7:00 p.m., 1st Floor, City Hall Community Room A, Inglewood City Hall One Manchester
  Boulevard, Inglewood, CA 90301

I. ADJOURNMENT
1. The Parking and Traffic Commission meeting ended at 8:15 PM PST.

J. ATTACHMENT
1. Attendance Sheet
